scope: Cocoa-led retained corpus aligned to manuscript gap and methods, with carefully labelled comparative coffee support
gap_questions: How strongly are international cocoa shocks transmitted to Colombian producer-linked prices once exchange-rate and oil conditions are taken into account?
Does the supply chain distribute adjustment unevenly, leaving producer-linked prices more exposed than downstream consumer prices?
How should localized weather variability enter the analysis: as a direct price driver or as contextual vulnerability that intensifies exposure?

papers.title: Trade Reforms and Integration of Cocoa Farmers into World Markets: Evidence from African and non-African Countries
papers.quote: the reforms have increased the exposure of farmers to world cocoa markets
papers.interpretation: The paper supports the claim that producer exposure rises when domestic cocoa markets are more tightly linked to world prices.

papers.title: The Effects of Dollar/Sterling Exchange Rate Volatility on Futures Markets for Coffee and Cocoa
papers.gap_role: exchange-rate channel in cocoa price dynamics
papers.quote: the exchange rate emerges as a main source of risk for the commodity futures price
papers.interpretation: The article supports modelling exchange-rate conditions as a distinct source of cocoa-market risk rather than background noise.

papers.title: Optimizing Cocoa Biomass Density through Integrated Irrigation and Drainage Management under Water Stress: A Linear Programming Approach
papers.gap_role: local weather architecture and variable selection
papers.quote: Using data from the NASA POWER database and incorporating detailed climate, soil, and crop management variables specific to San Vicente del Chucuri, Colombia
papers.interpretation: The paper supports the local choice of NASA POWER weather inputs and anchors the weather block in prior cocoa modelling for the same municipality.

papers.journal: International Journal of Biodiversity Science, Ecosystem Services & Management
papers.title: Unpacking 'sustainable' cocoa: do sustainability standards, development projects and policies address producer concerns in Indonesia, Cameroon and Peru?
papers.gap_role: producer constraints, weak market position, and institutional fit
papers.quote: Producers in all three countries shared concerns of price volatility, weak farmer organizations and dependence on few buyers.
papers.interpretation: This supports the manuscript's claim that cocoa vulnerability reflects both price instability and constrained producer capacity within the chain.

papers.title: Planning for Adaptation: A System Approach to Understand the Value Chain's Role in Supporting Smallholder Coffee Farmers' Adaptive Capacity in Peru
papers.gap_role: comparative tree-crop evidence on value-chain support
papers.quote: this study is the first to develop indicators that assess the sensitivity and adaptive capacity of coffee value-chain actors
papers.interpretation: Used carefully, this provides comparative evidence from a similar tropical tree-crop system that adaptive capacity depends on chain-level organization.

papers.title: An innovation perspective to climate change adaptation in coffee systems
papers.gap_role: comparative tree-crop evidence on adaptation systems
papers.quote: We identify climate change adaptation options, their scale of application, and the necessary implementation steps.
papers.interpretation: The paper is used only as comparative evidence that adaptation in similar perennial crop systems extends beyond the farm to wider organizational arrangements.

papers.title: Assessing Climate Smart Agriculture and Its Determinants of Practice in Ghana: A Case of the Cocoa Production System
papers.gap_role: climate vulnerability and adaptation in cocoa systems
papers.quote: enhance production, mitigate and/or remove GHG emissions and build resilience
papers.interpretation: The study supports treating resilience as an explicit analytical concern in cocoa systems rather than as an external framing device.

papers.title: Vulnerability to Climate Change of Cocoa in West Africa: Patterns, Opportunities and Limits to Adaptation
papers.gap_role: climatic suitability, adaptation limits, and spatial vulnerability
papers.quote: maximum dry season temperatures are projected to become as or more limiting for cocoa as dry season water availability
papers.interpretation: The article supports the claim that cocoa climate vulnerability is structured by specific biophysical constraints, not by generic climate stress alone.

papers.title: Climate risks to Brazilian coffee production
papers.quote: Negative climate hazard and exposure impacts for coffee producing regions could be potentially offset by targeting climate adaptation support to these high-risk regions
papers.interpretation: The paper is used only as comparative evidence that adaptation in similar perennial crop systems has a spatial risk dimension.

papers.title: Climate change adaptation of coffee production in space and time
papers.quote: to develop an adaptation framework across time and space to guide adaptation planning in Nicaraguan coffee systems
papers.interpretation: The article is used only as comparative evidence on spatially differentiated adaptation planning in a similar tropical perennial crop.

papers.title: Predicting the Future Climatic Suitability for Cocoa Farming of the World's Leading Producer Countries, Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire
papers.gap_role: future climatic suitability of cocoa-producing regions
papers.quote: we predict changes in relative climatic suitability for cocoa for 2050
papers.interpretation: The paper supports using climatic suitability as part of the vulnerability literature surrounding cocoa production.

papers.title: The physiological responses of cacao to the environment and the implications for climate change resilience. A review
papers.gap_role: physiological sensitivity to heat and water stress
papers.quote: water limitation causes significant yield reduction in cacao
papers.interpretation: The review supports incorporating weather as vulnerability context by showing clear physiological sensitivity to water stress.

papers.title: Agroecosystem resilience and farmers' perceptions of climate change impacts on cocoa farms in Alto Beni, Bolivia
papers.gap_role: agroecosystem resilience and cocoa farming systems
papers.quote: Agroecosystem resilience was higher under the two agroforestry systems than under common practice monoculture
papers.interpretation: The paper supports the argument that ecological design changes the buffering capacity of cocoa systems.

papers.title: Cocoa agroforestry systems versus monocultures: a multi-dimensional meta-analysis
papers.gap_role: agroforestry as adaptation and buffering strategy
papers.quote: Cocoa agroforestry contributed to climate change mitigation by storing 2.5 times more carbon and to adaptation by lowering mean temperatures
papers.interpretation: This directly supports the manuscript's treatment of agroforestry as a buffering mechanism under cocoa climate stress.

papers.title: Trade-offs between crop intensification and ecosystem services: the role of agroforestry in cocoa cultivation
papers.gap_role: interaction of price volatility, climate change, and ecological buffering
papers.quote: The removal of shade trees diminishes smallholders' ability to adapt to global change driven by demographic pressure, food insecurity, cocoa price volatility and climate change.
papers.interpretation: The article directly supports the manuscript's core claim that vulnerability is produced by market shocks interacting with limited buffering capacity.
